source_summaries.title: JVL Thinks the 2028 Republican Field Could Get REALLY Weird | Triad Mailbag
bullets: JVL and Jasmine Green discussed the dangers of extreme wealth concentration and the political influence of Silicon Valley billionaires.
The hosts evaluated whether the Republican establishment might support Donald Trump Jr. in 2028 to prevent a succession conflict.
The conversation also touched on constitutional reform, Democratic patriotism, and JVL's personal media consumption habits.

source_summaries.title: Jim Jordan Wants You to Forget Who He Is
bullets: House Republicans have selected Jim Jordan as their new leader following a major electoral defeat.
A historical review by Will Saletan details Jordan's extensive efforts to overturn the 2020 election, including promoting debunked voter fraud claims and pushing to discard electoral votes.
Jordan ultimately celebrated Donald Trump's pardons of January 6th defendants, and his party has rewarded him with a leadership position rather than reckoning with this history.

source_summaries.title: A Cruel Thanksgiving for the Kids Locked Up in Dilley
bullets: Staff at the Dilley family detention center taunted incarcerated children during holiday events by displaying food and gifts that were subsequently withheld from them.
Legal advocates and sworn parent declarations report that facility staff used detained children for staged holiday photo opportunities before leaving the minors in tears.
The Dilley facility has faced ongoing criticism for poor conditions, inadequate medical care, and exceeding the legal maximum detention time for children.

source_summaries.title: The Trio Reacts to Anthony Constantino’s Gay Republican Recruitment Video
bullets: Sam Stein, Tim Miller, and Will Sommer discuss Congressman-elect Anthony Constantino's recruitment video targeting gay Americans for the Republican party.
The podcast covers Megyn Kelly's claim that the MAGA movement is dead and a Trump loyalist's call for the president's resignation.
Former DOJ official Harmeet Dhillon addresses the Trump administration's troubling 'Groyper' issue.

source_summaries.title: Trump Plays Politics as Iowa Experiences a Toxic Explosion | Morning Shots
bullets: Andrew Egger and Bill Kristol discussed the controlled detonation of toxic military explosives in Iowa alongside the Trump administration's crisis management.
Stephen Miller's expanding influence over the federal government was highlighted in the discussion.
The conversation also covered Trump's continued push for tariffs amid inflation and emerging fractures in Republican loyalty due to the Nvidia scandal.

source_summaries.title: Thanksgiving and Nuclear War
bullets: Donald Trump announced a vision for a post-liberal world order where the US, Russia, and Xi's China cooperate to prevent liberal democracies from developing nuclear deterrents.
Ukrainian forces sank a Russian corvette off the coast of Libya using sea drones, demonstrating a new high-water mark for drone warfare 1,000 miles from the Ukrainian border.
The drone revolution threatens to neutralize traditional blue-water navies, potentially eliminating a key military differentiator that separates great powers from middle powers.

source_summaries.title: An Out-of-Control President Tries a Controlled Detonation
bullets: The U.S. military planned a controlled detonation of over 9,000 pounds of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant.
The operation raised public health concerns among local residents and environmental groups regarding toxic lead dust dispersion.
President Trump falsely blamed the Obama administration for the improper storage of explosives that date back to the 1980s.

source_summaries.title: The Hidden Message of ‘I Play Rocky’
bullets: The Bulwark podcast features an interview with Peter Gamble, the writer of the film 'I Play Rocky'.
The reviewer initially felt skeptical about a movie concerning the creation of 'Rocky' but ultimately found it delightful and engaging with audiences.
The film emphasizes themes of self-belief and mutual support while featuring a strong awards-season performance by Tracy Letts.

source_summaries.title: Slow Boring candidates won the midterms
bullets: Candidates supported by the Slow Boring slate mostly won during the recent midterm elections.
The electoral performance reflects a national political climate that was significantly bluer than public polling indicated.
The primary goal of the Slow Boring slate is to develop a pipeline of pragmatic, culturally moderate, and pro-growth Democrats.

source_summaries.title: REPLAY: Is America Losing Its Scientific Edge? — with Dr. Shruti Naik & Kristin O'Donoghue
bullets: Prof G Media research analyst Kristin O’Donoghue examines how cuts to federal funding are affecting America's scientific engine.
Dr. Shruti Naik discusses the practical impacts on her lab and patients suffering from autoimmune diseases.
Dr. Naik maintains her belief that American scientific institutions remain exceptional despite current funding challenges.

source_summaries.title: Anthropic’s IPO Is Already Underwater
bullets: Ed Elson and George Noble discuss Anthropic's recent IPO and its implications for OpenAI.
The discussion advises investors to look past day-to-day market volatility.
Charles Elson examines corporate governance failures related to the Nvidia scandal.

source_summaries.title: Who Actually Makes Money in the Creator Economy?
bullets: Advertisers are increasingly investing in content creators despite the reality that very few creators earn enough to quit their traditional jobs.
Derek Thompson successfully transitioned from a traditional media salary to a lucrative independent business model through Substack.
Subscription-based revenue models can significantly increase the overall financial valuation of media companies like Prof G Media.

source_summaries.title: Fusion’s Kitty Hawk.
bullets: Commonwealth Fusion Systems plans to activate its SPARC machine in 2027 to demonstrate net-positive fusion energy.
OpenAI announced that its latest language models have successfully designed new proteins, sparking debate over biological AI capabilities.
Internal unreleased AI models are becoming so powerful that some employees question their safety and control.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned of potential nightmare scenarios involving rogue AI agent botnets taking down segments of the internet.

source_summaries.title: FDA to Expand Prescription Drug Testing After ProPublica Revealed Safety Concerns
bullets: The FDA is expanding its program to test prescription drugs for impurities and quality lapses following safety concerns raised by ProPublica.
The agency will purchase medications from retail pharmacies and wholesale distributors to test them more frequently and identify poorly performing drugs.
Drug-safety experts praise the expansion as a critical step to address long-standing concerns regarding the oversight of foreign and domestic generic drug manufacturers.

source_summaries.title: Democrats Vow to Shield Smithsonian From Any Trump Overhaul
bullets: A top congressional Democrat announced an investigation into leaked White House plans to overhaul the Smithsonian Institution's leadership and exhibits.
The drafted proposals, accidentally photographed on a commuter train, included replacing top museum officials and introducing new Washington-centric exhibits.
Lawmakers and Smithsonian leadership emphasized the institution's independence and vowed to resist political interference.

source_summaries.title: Oregon Housing Leader Met With Officials Who Are Seeking Money for a Project Her Husband’s Employer Is Developing
bullets: Oregon housing official Andrea Bell was personally involved in discussions about state funding for an apartment project that her husband's employer is helping to develop.
Records show a financial connection between housing council decisions and Bell's husband's firm, which stands to earn millions in fees if funding transactions close.
Ethics experts state that Bell should have reported a potential conflict of interest to the governor and recused herself from related project discussions.

source_summaries.title: An Alarming Spike in Ectopic Pregnancy Deaths Was Hiding in Plain Sight in a Federal Dataset
bullets: Ectopic pregnancy deaths in the United States have nearly doubled in recent years, with a particularly stark increase in states enforcing strict abortion bans.
Federal and state governments, as well as leading maternal health experts, failed to publicly identify or track this alarming mortality trend prior to recent investigative analysis.
Ectopic pregnancies represent a leading cause of first-trimester maternal death, yet federal agencies do not comprehensively track their overall incidence or require systematic reporting.

source_summaries.title: Court to hear argument on whether school employees may bring suit under Title IX
bullets: The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on whether school employees can file sex discrimination lawsuits under Title IX or if they must use Title VII.
Two former Georgia university employees appealed an 11th Circuit ruling which held that Title IX does not provide employees a private right to sue.
The plaintiffs argue that Title IX's broad text and past court precedents permit employee lawsuits, while the university system contends the statute does not authorize private suits for employees.

source_summaries.title: Justices to consider whether noncitizens who lose asylum status may still obtain green cards
bullets: The Supreme Court is set to hear oral arguments in Wassily v. Blanche to determine if noncitizens who lose their asylum status remain eligible to obtain green cards.
The case involves two men whose asylum protections were terminated following criminal convictions and who subsequently applied for lawful permanent residency.
The central legal question is whether the statutory phrase 'granted asylum' refers strictly to a continuing present status or to a past, historical event.

source_summaries.title: Heading into the Thanksgiving break
bullets: The Supreme Court's December argument session begins on Monday, November 30, with eight total oral arguments scheduled.
The justices dismissed the lead plaintiff in the AR-15 ban case, now renamed Khaya v. Cook County, and deferred action on mootness until after oral arguments on December 2.
Catholic schools have petitioned the Supreme Court to challenge Maine rules regarding public funding exclusions and to potentially overrule Employment Division v. Smith.

source_summaries.title: U.S. Announces New Tariffs on 14 Major Trading Partners, Including China and the EU
bullets: The Trump administration proposed new tariffs on 14 major trading partners, including China and the European Union, targeting alleged unfair industrial practices and excess production capacity.

The measures utilize Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 following a Supreme Court ruling against previous emergency powers, with implementation potentially delayed until January 2027 pending public hearings.
China faces the highest proposed duties of up to an additional 20%, while the tariffs risk increasing import costs and consumer prices amid a reported U.S. inflation rate of 3.8%.

source_summaries.title: What Nvidia-Gate Tells Us About Trump
bullets: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following reports of an extramarital affair with a corporate executive identified by U.S. officials as a Chinese intelligence asset.
President Trump pressured Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang, personally calling into a board meeting to advocate for his return.
Huang was successfully reinstated, leading to a record-breaking single-day stock increase for Nvidia that personally profited Trump through his shareholdings.

source_summaries.title: Grand Theft Autocrat
bullets: The publication features political cartoons by Marian Kamensky, Badiucao, and Emanuele Del Rosso focusing on a Trump-Xi-Putin summit.
Ruth Ben-Ghiat highlights the role of humor and laughtivism as effective tools for mobilization and civic education against authoritarianism.

source_summaries.title: 💬 New thread from Sonny Bunch
bullets: Sonny Bunch hosted a subscriber chat on The Bulwark to discuss Thanksgiving viewing recommendations, new theatrical releases, and VOD titles.
The discussion highlighted recent films including James Gray's Paper Tiger and I Play Rocky.
Bunch also shared a previously published piece featuring suggestions for Thanksgiving-themed movies.

source_summaries.source: Phillips P. OBrien and Oleksiy Moskalenko from Phillips’s
source_summaries.title: Live with Phillips P. OBrien and Oleksiy Moskalenko
bullets: Phillips P. OBrien and Oleksiy Moskalenko hosted a live video session on November 25, 2026.
A 46-minute recording of the live event was made available for subscribers to watch.

source_summaries.title: Recommendations from your Substacks
bullets: The article compiles recommendations from subscribed Substacks for the week.
Featured newsletters include Can We Still Govern?, The Recombobulation Area, and The Present Age.
It highlights content and publications from writers such as Radley Balko, Dan Shafer, and Parker Molloy.

source_summaries.title: Community Black Friday: 40% off Agent Engineering + a year of Mentorship
bullets: Learn AI Together is offering a Black Friday promotion with 40 percent off its Agent Engineering course and a year of mentorship.
The discounted package is available for $719.40 instead of $1,398 until December 6 using a specific promo code.
The offering includes access to senior engineers for questions, live calls, production blueprints, and career profile reviews.

source_summaries.title: The Big Splat
bullets: Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia following intervention from Donald Trump and tech elites who claimed elite impunity was essential for the stock market.
Proponents of Huang's return argued that holding billionaires accountable would cause the U.S. technology sector to implode.
The surge in stock prices following the reinstatement proved to be temporary, as AI and tech stocks quickly returned to their pre-announcement levels.

source_summaries.title: This Thanksgiving, Americans are more worried about the bill than their uncle’s politics
bullets: Eighty-three percent of Americans plan to participate in a home-cooked Thanksgiving meal, though demographic differences exist across education levels, age groups, and political affiliations.
Sixty percent of respondents expect politics to be discussed during Thanksgiving dinner, with partisans showing more eagerness for the conversation than independents.

source_summaries.source: Kira Tebbe and Sarah Esty from Can We Still Govern?
source_summaries.title: The Looming SNAP Crisis No One Is Talking About
bullets: State systems administering SNAP are facing operational collapse due to an unprecedented accumulation of major federal policy directives and funding cuts over a two-year period.

Recent federal rules and changes—including expanded work requirements, payment error cost shares, administrative funding reductions, and proposed rollbacks of categorical eligibility—threaten the program's stability.
The relentless volume of simultaneous changes has severely strained state IT systems, administrative resources, and frontline staff, jeopardizing the basic functioning of the SNAP program.

source_summaries.title: Can You Be Thankful When Putin Is Trying To Kill You?
bullets: Garry Kasparov reflects on finding gratitude during Thanksgiving despite facing a targeted assassination plot by Russian intelligence services.
He notes that Thanksgiving was formalized as a national holiday by Abraham Lincoln in 1863 during the height of the American Civil War.
Instead of dwelling on security threats and hardships, Kasparov expresses thankfulness for his family, supporters, meaningful work, and raising his children in a free country.

source_summaries.title: Taking a Few Days Off
bullets: The author announced a temporary break from publishing.
Regular posting will resume after the holiday food coma.

source_summaries.title: Why this lead explosion in Iowa is so maddening
bullets: The U.S. military is detonating approximately 9,500 pounds of unstable lead azide near Middletown, Iowa, releasing a potential plume of toxic lead dust over Iowa and Missouri.
Lead is a severe neurotoxin with no safe exposure level, posing permanent developmental risks to children and dangers to pregnant individuals.
The operation has sparked public frustration and fear due to poor management, late notifications, and shifting dispersion models leaving residents scrambling.

source_summaries.title: The extremely sordid resurrection of Jensen Huang
bullets: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following a scandal involving a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, only to be reinstated eleven days later due to direct pressure from President Trump.
President Trump openly acknowledged that his intervention was crucial in forcing the company's board to restore Huang to his position.
The administration was previously warned about Huang through classified intelligence memos from Secretary of State Marco Rubio, which both Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick largely ignored.

source_summaries.source: Michael Spencer and Jenny Ouyang from AI Supremacy
source_summaries.title: Claude 2.0: The Feature Changes That Overturn How You Work
bullets: Anthropic is facing financial pressures as its stock price has dropped below its initial public offering price.
Internal models are becoming so powerful that some employees reportedly doubt they can be safely released.
Generative AI models are accelerating cybersecurity vulnerabilities and creating real-world structural crises.

source_summaries.title: The Trump Administration Is Pulling Out The Stops (For Putin)
bullets: The Trump administration is actively shifting its approach to benefit Vladimir Putin, according to the article.
Jared Kushner and other administration figures have notably changed their public messaging regarding Ukraine and Russia.
Ukrainian leadership and observers appear to be finally recognizing these dramatic behavioral shifts from Washington.

source_summaries.title: Office Hours: What Are You Most Grateful For?
bullets: Robert Reich published an Office Hours column ahead of Thanksgiving inviting readers to share what they are most grateful for.
The author collected and categorized responses from colleagues, friends, and acquaintances regarding their current sources of gratitude.
The full content of the post and its discussion categories require a paid subscription to access.
